gemini_response.public_law_citation: Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (Dec. 23, 2022)
gemini_response.threshold_adjustment_method: Calculated annually based on 130% of the Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH) for a military member in pay grade E-5 with dependents for the military housing area with the highest BAH in the United States.
gemini_response.core_protection: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence, for which the monthly rent is below the statutory threshold, without first obtaining a court order.
gemini_response.covered_persons: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
gemini_response.recent_amendments: The Veterans Auto and Education Improvement Act of 2022 (enacted as part of the FY23 National Defense Authorization Act) significantly amended 50 U.S.C. § 3951(a)(2). It replaced the former fixed-dollar rent threshold (which was adjusted for CPI) with a new formula based on the Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH). This change substantially increased the dollar value of the rent threshold, expanding the number of protected leases.
gemini_response.notes: The statutory threshold is a *monthly* rent figure, not an annual one. The affidavit requirement under 50 U.S.C. § 3931 applies broadly to civil actions where a servicemember defendant has not made an appearance, requiring the plaintiff to attest to the defendant's military status before a default judgment may be entered. Upon application by the servicemember, a court may stay the eviction proceeding for 90 days or adjust the lease obligations if it finds the servicemember's ability to pay is materially affected by military service.
